Everything you need to ship from India to Uruguay or import from Uruguay to India: the trade agreement, routes and transit times, how your buyer imports, duties, regulators and documents.
India and Uruguay at a glance
India–Mercosur Preferential Trade Agreement (in force since 2009). Uruguay is among the members pushing to expand it; expansion talks launched in September 2026.
India exports vehicles, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, textiles and engineering goods. India buys wood pulp, wool, timber and soya products.
Routes and transit times to Uruguay
35–45 days to Montevideo. Direct East Coast South America services from Nhava Sheva/Mundra (around the Cape of Good Hope), or transhipment via Colombo, Singapore or Jebel Ali.
Transit times are indicative port-to-port from Nhava Sheva / Mundra (sea) and Delhi / Mumbai (air). Routing changes (for example Red Sea diversions) can add 10–14 days.
Importing into Uruguay: what your buyer needs
A licensed customs broker (despachante de aduana) is mandatory.
Free zones and the free-port regime make Montevideo a regional distribution hub for Mercosur.
Mercosur TEC, plus 22% VAT (IVA) and advance tax payments.

From Uruguay to India, and tips from the field
Pulp and wool are the main flows.
File the Bill of Entry through a licensed customs broker in India (YAM holds licence R-7/92).
Check the HS code in the Indian tariff, the DGFT import policy (free, restricted or prohibited) and any BIS, FSSAI, plant quarantine or other permit before the goods ship.
If an agreement applies, get the correct certificate of origin from the exporter to claim the lower duty.
Use Montevideo free zones to hold stock for Argentina, Paraguay and southern Brazil.
